data.long_meaning: Ishant is a compound name derived from two words: 'Ish' and 'An'. Ish means God, while An means protection. Thus, Ishant means 'God of Protection'.

The name resonates deeply with both the optimistic and the fearful, offering a reassuring sense of security, and represents the benevolent aspect of Hindu gods who protect their devotees. Furthermore, the name Ishant is also used as a personal name for boys, making it a popular choice in Hindu communities.

Ishant is an eternal reminder that even in the darkest of times, amidst trials and tribulations, one can always find solace and refuge in the loving embrace of God. It shows us that even when we live in challenging circumstances, we should never forget the presence of our divine protectors. This name can act as a constant motivation to seek refuge, comfort, and strength in the divine. historical_references.reference: Ishant is a name of Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction. He is also known as Ishana, Rudra, and Mahadeva. Ishant is often depicted with multiple arms, each holding various weapons, and a third eye on his forehead. He is the supreme lord, the ultimate reality, and the creator, destroyer, and preserver of the universe.

The name Ishant is also mentioned in Mahabharata, the great Indian epic. In this text, Ishant is the name of a celestial being who is a messenger of Shiva. He is sent to the battlefield of Kurukshetra to help the Pandava prince Bhima in his fight against the Kaurava prince Duryodhana.
